podcast: Chatting with The Experts with Paula Okonneh

8813f7c0d5.q: Why do high-achieving women struggle with execution and procrastination according to the 90 Day Wins approach?
8813f7c0d5.a: High-achieving women often help other people achieve their goals and make their own goals an afterthought, which is where procrastination comes in. They need to understand that what they want is important and give it time. Many women are helping others succeed while putting themselves last, and they don't realize they can choose to move past procrastination by being intentional about their own priorities.
8813f7c0d5.rq: You can choose to beat it. You can choose to move past it. But it starts with you understanding that what you want is important. So you have to give it some time.

9233b100c8.q: What is the 90 Day Wins framework and why is the 90-day timeframe specifically chosen?
9233b100c8.a: The 90 Day Wins framework breaks goals into manageable quarterly, monthly, and weekly steps. The 90-day timeframe was chosen because people can relate to it through job probation periods and corporate quarterly reporting cycles. By breaking down a vision into smaller steps over 90 days, people can track progress and celebrate wins without feeling overwhelmed, and working with accountability partners in the Win Collective community helps keep people motivated.
9233b100c8.rq: You can choose to beat it. You can choose to move past it. But it starts with you understanding that what you want is important. So you have to give it some time.

b96696ccf5.q: How can perfectionism and waiting for the right time prevent people from starting their projects?
b96696ccf5.a: Perfectionism and waiting for the right time are common blockers because people think everything must be perfect before launching. Sandra compares it to software companies that push out updates knowing they are not perfect, then send patches to fix issues. She emphasizes that it is important to start and make changes along the way, like how her first podcast episodes showed she was just starting out but by episode 50 and 100 she had tweaked things and improved.
b96696ccf5.rq: You can choose to beat it. You can choose to move past it. But it starts with you understanding that what you want is important. So you have to give it some time.

0086aaac3c.q: How does saying no to distractions and 'locking in' help people achieve their 90-day goals?
0086aaac3c.a: Locking in means being intentional about time and refusing distractions from things that do not align with current priorities. Sandra has had to say no to networking events and meetings about new social media trends to focus on her execution journal and personal goals. She prioritizes doing what needs to be done first, then enjoys social activities afterward, because she knows what it feels like to have regret from spending time on distractions instead of goals.
0086aaac3c.rq: You can choose to beat it. You can choose to move past it. But it starts with you understanding that what you want is important. So you have to give it some time.

16141392c8.q: What real-world example does Sandra share about someone who achieved a goal in 90 days using her method?
16141392c8.a: A truck driver on leave at a farm in Atlanta wanted to create socks and had design ideas. Over 90 days, he called foreign companies and executed his plans with weekly accountability meetings with Sandra. At the end of 90 days, he was holding his completed socks. He later expanded to creating tights for women. Sandra emphasizes that he succeeded not because he knew everything about sock creation, but because he was teachable, open to possibilities, and had someone to keep him accountable weekly.
16141392c8.rq: You can choose to beat it. You can choose to move past it. But it starts with you understanding that what you want is important. So you have to give it some time.
